sections.h2: Where Craven County deeds are recorded
sections.html:
Land documents here go to 226 Pollock Street, New Bern, ZIP 28560. Reach the office at 252-636-6617. State law makes the register one of three county-wide elected offices.

On the land side the office handles deeds, deeds of trust, plats, maps and every other instrument touching real property. Staff also keep vital records and military discharges and issue marriage licenses and assumed business names. Records go back more than three centuries, so an old family tract can be traced at the same office that records a current sale.

What matters most to a seller is the cutoff. Recording stops at 4:30 p.m., and notaries are not sworn in after that hour either. A late funding would be filed the next business day, so ask your closing office how it plans for that.

Fifteen pages of an ordinary deed run $26, then $4 a page. A deed of trust runs $64 for 35 pages and $4 for every page beyond.

Craven County land record charges

Copies, vital records and marriage licenses can be paid for with cash, check or card; call about any other payment type. A $3.50 convenience fee applies to online vital-record orders through the county's vendor, but not to a real estate recording.

sections.h2: Who pays the deed excise tax
sections.html:
This one is the seller's. G.S. 105-228.30 makes the transferor pay the register ahead of filing, at one dollar per $500 of price or value.

  • A leftover fraction of $500 is treated as a whole $500.
  • Half the money stays in the county's general fund; half goes to the state.
  • It follows the deed's stated consideration or value and is listed among the seller's charges on the settlement statement.

Your closing attorney will work out the exact dollars. The result can differ from a quick estimate from the price when the price is not the full value of what changes hands.

Three tools sit on the Real Estate page of the register's site: an e-recording partner page, a public records search and a UCC filings page. The sidebar also carries a Recordation Notification link, whose coverage the office can explain.

Lenders and closing offices that send many documents are the natural users of e-recording, and with an attorney handling your closing you will rarely file anything yourself. Mailed UCC filings need a check made out to Register of Deeds at the Pollock Street address.

  • Find your vesting deed through the online search and compare its legal description with what you plan to convey.
  • Before listing, scan for any deed of trust lacking a satisfaction.
  • If the house was inherited, ask what the office keeps under the wills and divorce decrees pages in its menu.

sections.h2: What registration does to your title
sections.html:
Registration sets priority. G.S. 47-18 denies protection to an unregistered deed, option, lease over three years or right of first refusal against lien creditors and purchasers for value, with competing claims ranked by registration time.

Sellers should ask for proof of recording once the funds move. The release of an old mortgage works the same way. Recording a satisfaction is free, so verify that a paid-off loan no longer appears as open on the index.

Chapter 47H, on contracts for deed, adds its own recording duty. The seller must file the contract or a memorandum inside five business days, the buyer may cancel during three business days, and forfeiture needs written notice with at least 30 days to cure. Read that chapter first if you plan to finance a buyer.

sections.h2: Checklist before the deed is filed
sections.html:
Look over the register's index and fee schedule before closing; problems found now are cheaper than problems found after funding.

  • See that the index lists your vesting deed under the name you are selling in, with a legal description that agrees with the survey or tax record.
  • Match every deed of trust with a satisfaction. Because satisfactions cost nothing to record, a payoff lender has no fee reason to hold one back.
  • Count the deed's pages: $4 more per page after 15, or after 35 for a deed of trust.
  • Ask whether the instrument is non-standard, which carries a $25 fee, or whether several recordings are bundled in one document, which adds $10 for separate indexing.
  • Get the current-year payoff from Tax Collection so no bill stays open after the title changes hands.

Your closing attorney sees the whole title picture and should have the last word, but these items give you questions to ask.

sections.h2: If you file the deed yourself
sections.html:
Few Craven County sellers ever carry a deed to the counter, but some transfers happen without a closing office. If yours does, bring the signed original, the fee for its page count and the excise tax. Get there before 4:30 p.m. for same-day recording; anything later is recorded the next business day.

Review the layout first, since a non-standard document costs $25 extra and bundled recordings add $10 for separate indexing. Afterward, search the online records to confirm the deed is indexed under the right names, and file the recording details with your closing papers.

Planning moved the county's Community Rating System class from 8 to 7, lifting the flood insurance premium discount for owners in unincorporated areas from 10% to 15%. A buyer's insurance agent can say what applies at a specific address.

Tax bills are separate from the register. Payment is due September 1, and interest holds off until after January 5. Ask the Tax Collection Division, 252-636-6605, for a payoff figure ahead of closing so the bill is cleared by the time the deed goes on record.

If a home faces tax foreclosure, the county's foreclosure page lists properties for sale and gives the tax collection email for questions. Listed properties are not owned by the county, and owners are pointed to a state homeowner assistance site for delinquent tax help. If you would rather skip repairs and delays, our North Carolina page describes a cash sale.

Craven County is mid-sized and growing: roughly 105,025 residents now against 100,720 at the 2020 count, living in 50,334 housing units. The median owner-occupied value was $231,600 for 2020 to 2024, with 68.4% of homes owner-held, and 553 building permits were issued in 2025. Eight towns, Bridgeton through Vanceboro, lie within its borders, so a town levy may apply to your parcel; the tax office can tell you.

faqs.q: Where does a Craven County deed get filed?
faqs.a: In New Bern, at the register's Pollock Street office. Recording ends at 4:30 p.m., so ask your closing office how a later deed is handled.

faqs.q: What is the price of recording a Craven deed?
faqs.a: $26 for fifteen pages plus $4 per extra page. A deed of trust is $64 for 35 pages.

faqs.q: Does filing a mortgage satisfaction cost anything in Craven County?
faqs.a: No. A satisfaction of deed of trust is recorded at no charge.

faqs.q: Who covers excise tax on a Craven sale?
faqs.a: The seller. It goes to the register ahead of filing at $1 per $500 of consideration, with a partial $500 counted in full.

faqs.q: Can I look up Craven deeds from home?
faqs.a: Yes. The register links an online public records search, and its Real Estate page covers e-recording partners.
